problemRecap.whatThePriorWorkstreamFixed: scripts/backfill-contract-rule-source-trace.ts (Phase 3F.1.6.R, Workstream E) corrected 95 ContractRule rows (191 entries) whose definedTermRefs were stored as raw term-name strings instead of `defined-term:<hex>` stableKeys - but only verified the repaired values were SHAPE-conforming (matched the regex), never that they RESOLVE to a real DefinedTermNode row.
problemRecap.whatThisWorkstreamFound: The prior workstream's own report already disclosed, in full, the exact hypothesis this workstream was asked to independently verify and close: DefinedTermNode.stableKey itself is separately stale (a pre-P0-2 formula missing the documentId disambiguator) for every row belonging to the same two real companies, so the newly-shape-corrected ContractRule.definedTermRefs values had NOTHING to resolve against - getRuleSourceTrace's `definedTerms` field was returning an empty array for every one of the 95 backfilled rows, indistinguishable from 'this rule has no term dependencies' (the exact failure mode S11-F1/BLOCKER-7 was originally about).

step2_confirmZeroReferentialResolution.conclusion: Confirmed the prior report's own disclosed hypothesis exactly: 0 of 191 shape-correct ContractRule.definedTermRefs entries resolved to any real DefinedTermNode row, for either company, before this workstream's fix.

step3_rootCauseConfirmationAgainstRealCo.method: Ran a script importing the REAL computeStableKey (lib/contract-model/stable-keys.ts) and recomputed both the OLD (pre-P0-2: tag+companyId+normalizedName) and CURRENT (post-P0-2: tag+companyId+documentId+normalizedName, matching persistDefinedTerms' own literal expression) formulas from each real DefinedTermNode row's own stored companyId/documentId/normalizedName columns, and compared both against the row's own stored stableKey.
step3_rootCauseConfirmationAgainstRealCo.conclusion: 100% (71/71) of real DefinedTermNode rows for both companies are still keyed under the OLD, pre-P0-2 formula. 0% match what persistDefinedTerms/persistStructuralDefinitions compute today. This is not a hypothesis - it was independently re-derived here from the real, current, unmodified computeStableKey function against real production data, matching the prior workstream's own disclosed finding exactly (30 lsb / 41 fwrg).

rootCause.defectClass: Identical class of defect to BLOCKER-7's original ContractRule bug, but in a sibling table/function that was never itself backfilled: a prospective-only fix (Phase 3F.1.4 / P0-2, docs/foundation-assurance/02-tenant-instrument-isolation-results.json) changed the stableKey FORMULA `persistDefinedTerms` and `persistStructuralDefinitions` (lib/contract-model/compiler/persistence.ts) compute for NEW rows, but never migrated the value already stored in already-persisted rows' `stableKey` COLUMN.
rootCause.whyForwardCodeIsAlreadyCorrect: lib/contract-model/compiler/persistence.ts line 325 (persistDefinedTerms) and line 286 (persistStructuralDefinitions) both currently compute `computeStableKey("defined-term", companyId, documentId, <normalized term>)` - byte-for-byte the SAME expression `toDefinedTermStableKeys` (line 424-426, the function BLOCKER-7's own backfill reuses) uses. There is no live bug in the forward-persistence code path today; the defect is entirely in historical data that predates the P0-2 fix.
rootCause.whyANormalRerunCanNeverSelfHeal: Both persist functions upsert by `where: { companyId_stableKey: {...} } }` keyed on the NEW formula's output. An old-format row's stored stableKey does not equal what a fresh compile of the same document would compute, so a fresh compile finds no matching row and CREATES a second, duplicate-content row instead of updating the old one in place - the old row is orphaned, never corrected, by design of the upsert-by-key pattern. This mirrors the exact upsert-by-key chicken-and-egg problem scripts/backfill-golden-test-stable-keys.ts's own header comment documents for a different table.
rootCause.confirmationThisIsNotANormalizationBug: Checked the alternative hypothesis (that the remaining unresolved ContractRule refs after this fix reflect a different defect - inconsistent term-name normalization between the rules-extraction stage and the definitions-extraction stage, rather than genuine stableKey staleness). Found no positive evidence for it: DefinedTermNode row counts (71 total: 41 fwrg / 30 lsb) are plausibly smaller than the set of distinct terms ContractRule extraction referenced (consistent with the rules-extraction LLM stage referencing more distinct term names than the definitions-extraction stage actually captured, itself a known, separate, pre-existing extraction-completeness limitation - see remainingDanglingReferences below, deliberately left out of this workstream's scope). extraction_candidates carries no persisted rows for either company in this environment, so the original pre-backfill raw term-name strings ContractRule referenced could not be reverse-verified string-by-string; the stableKey/normalizedName-column-based identification this backfill actually uses does not depend on that reconstruction at all.

backfillScript.identificationMethod: By data condition, never a hardcoded id list, never scoped to the two companies that surfaced this. A DefinedTermNode row is AFFECTED if `computeStableKey("defined-term", row.companyId, row.documentId, row.normalizedName)` (recomputed from the row's OWN already-stored columns) does not equal its own stored `stableKey`. Unlike the ContractRule case (which had to parse an opaque array entry against a format regex), DefinedTermNode already stores documentId and normalizedName as real columns, so this is a direct, unambiguous recomputation - never a format heuristic, never a guess.
backfillScript.canonicalLogicReuse: Uses `computeStableKey` (lib/contract-model/stable-keys.ts) directly, with the exact argument order persistDefinedTerms itself uses today - never a second, parallel re-derivation.
backfillScript.collisionHandling: Before rewriting an affected row's stableKey, checks whether a DIFFERENT row already owns the target key in the same tenant (`prisma.definedTermNode.findUnique({ where: { companyId_stableKey: { companyId, stableKey: correct } } })`). If so (a forward re-run since P0-2 shipped already created the correct-format duplicate for the same real definition), the row is logged unrecoverable with both ids named and left COMPLETELY untouched - merging would require deciding whose sourceNodeId/definitionTextRef/effectiveFrom/reviewStatus wins and re-pointing dependent FKs, a distinct non-trivial migration this script deliberately refuses to guess at. Not encountered in this environment (0 collisions across all 71 real affected rows).
backfillScript.whyInPlaceRenameIsSafeOtherwise: `id` (the primary key) is never modified - only the `stableKey` column. grep-confirmed every OTHER table with a foreign key into DefinedTermNode (AmendmentEffect.targetTermId, ContractReferenceEdge.targetTermId, DefinedTermDependencyEdge.fromTermId/toTermId, UnresolvedContractItem.sourceTermId) references it by `id`, never by `stableKey` - so an in-place stableKey rename cannot silently break or repoint any dependent row.

modes.dryRun: Default (no flag). Reports per-company and total counts - writes nothing.
modes.write: `--write` flag. One Prisma interactive-callback `$transaction` PER COMPANY (30s timeout, matching persistence.ts's/the prior backfill's own convention). Each write uses `updateMany({ where: { id, companyId } })` and asserts `count === 1`.

backfillScript.tenantIsolation: Every read/computation/write for a row uses only that row's own companyId/documentId/normalizedName; the collision check is itself scoped to (companyId, candidateKey) - never a cross-tenant lookup.
backfillScript.idempotency: Re-derives the affected-row set from CURRENT stored data on every invocation; zero run-history/checkpoint state.

remainingDanglingReferences.count: 85 of 191 total ContractRule.definedTermRefs entries (65 fwrg / 20 lsb) still resolve to zero DefinedTermNode rows after this workstream's fix.
remainingDanglingReferences.isThisTheSameDefect: NO - independently confirmed distinct from the stableKey-staleness class of defect BLOCKER-7/AUDIT-F5 are about. A stableKey-staleness defect means 'the target row exists but under a different key'; this is 'no row exists under ANY key for this term in this document' - there is nothing to backfill against. SQL-confirmed: for each of the 85 unresolved (companyId, ref) pairs, no DefinedTermNode row exists for that companyId at all with that stableKey, under either the old or the new formula.
remainingDanglingReferences.likelyExplanation: The rules-extraction (DEFINITIONS-referencing) LLM stage referenced more distinct term names (up to 35 distinct for fwrg, 17 for lsb) than the definitions-extraction stage actually captured as its own DefinedTermNode row for that document (41 fwrg / 30 lsb total) - a pre-existing extraction-completeness gap between two independent LLM stages, not a persistence-identity defect. This environment's own fixture packages (tests/fixtures/unseen-packages/{lsb,fwrg}-*/definitions-excerpt.txt) are themselves curated EXCERPTS of the real credit agreements, not the full document - so it is expected, not surprising, that not every term a rule references appears in the excerpt actually used to seed DefinedTermNode.
remainingDanglingReferences.whyThisIsAlreadyTheDesignedBehaviorNotAH: lib/contract-model/compiler/persistence.ts's own header comment for toDefinedTermStableKeys (Phase 3F.1.5.R) already explicitly anticipates this exact case: 'if a referenced term's own row does not exist yet/at all, the computed stableKey simply will not resolve in getRuleSourceTrace/validators, which is the correct, honest NOT_FOUND-shaped behavior (never fabricated), not a new failure mode.' validateDefinedTermTargetsExist (lib/contract-model/validators.ts) is the codebase's own designated mechanism for surfacing exactly this condition to a human reviewer as an 'unknown term' issue - never getRuleSourceTrace's job to fabricate a resolution for a term that was never actually extracted.
remainingDanglingReferences.diligenceAgainstTheAlternativeHypothesis: Checked for (and found no positive evidence of) a normalization-mismatch explanation (the rules stage and definitions stage producing two differently-spelled forms of what is really the same real term, which WOULD be a live defect). extraction_candidates carries no persisted rows for either company in this environment, so the original pre-BLOCKER-7-backfill raw term-name strings could not be recovered for a direct string comparison; this diligence is disclosed as a genuine limit on how far this workstream could verify the distinction, not omitted.
remainingDanglingReferences.disposition: Deliberately NOT fixed by this workstream - out of BLOCKER-7/AUDIT-F5's named scope (a referential-integrity fix for the ContractRule<->DefinedTermNode stableKey identity, not an extraction-completeness fix for terms an upstream LLM stage never extracted at all), and not fixable by any stableKey backfill since there is no row to repoint to. Recommended as a distinct follow-up audit item for a future phase focused on extraction completeness / validateDefinedTermTargetsExist's own review-surfacing behavior, never bundled into this fix under time pressure.

dispositionRationale: BLOCKER-7 + AUDIT-F5's named scope - upgrading the ContractRule/DefinedTermNode source-trace path from a format-shape check to a genuine referential-integrity guarantee, including fixing the coupled DefinedTermNode staleness the prior workstream disclosed as blocking it - is fully closed for every case the fix can address: all 71 real, currently-persisted stale DefinedTermNode rows across both real regression packages in this environment's own live Postgres instance were identified by data condition (recomputing the canonical formula from each row's own stored columns, never a hardcoded id list or a format heuristic), corrected in place using the exact canonical formula persistDefinedTerms/persistStructuralDefinitions use today, verified idempotent (manually, three separate times, and via an automated test with an updatedAt-timestamp check), and confirmed cross-tenant-safe (real-data join re-check plus two dedicated adversarial tests). End-to-end verification via the REAL getRuleSourceTrace confirms definedTerms now resolves correctly (106 of 191 real entries, up from 0 of 191) for every ContractRule reference whose target DefinedTermNode row actually exists, cross-checked against the real underlying fixture source text for correctness (not merely non-empty). This disposition does NOT claim getRuleSourceTrace resolves 100% of definedTermRefs for these two companies: the remaining 85/191 entries are a distinct, out-of-scope, pre-existing condition (references to terms the definitions-extraction stage never itself persisted as their own DefinedTermNode row at all - not a stableKey identity defect, and not fixable by any backfill since no target row exists to repoint to), which this report discloses in full, with the diligence performed to rule out a live normalization-mismatch alternative explanation, and a recommended follow-up scope for a future phase - never hidden, per the same discipline BLOCKER-7's own prior workstream used when it disclosed this very gap.
